scenes.tts: Buri kept sixteen fruit flies as the parents of every generation. He ran one hundred and seven bottles. In every bottle, two alleles of the brown eye colour locus began at the same frequency, zero point five. After nineteen generations, many bottles held only one allele. Nobody chose which allele won.

scenes.tts: Think of an election poll. Ask twenty people, and the result can be far from the true vote. Nobody biased the small poll. It was just small. Each generation is a poll of the one before. The offspring carry a random sample of the parents' gene copies. That chance change in allele frequency is genetic drift. It needs no difference in fitness.

scenes.tts: Gene flow is the movement of alleles between populations. It pulls their frequencies toward each other. Say residents carry an allele at zero point six, and immigrants at zero point two. If immigrants are one tenth of the breeding pool, the mixed frequency is zero point five six. That drop of zero point zero four is deterministic. It would happen the same way every time. Whether gene flow helps or harms depends on what the new alleles do in the new place.
scenes.caption: Gene flow is the movement of alleles between populations. It pulls their frequencies toward each other. Say residents carry an allele at 0.6, and immigrants at 0.2. If immigrants are one tenth of the breeding pool, the mixed frequency is 0.56. That drop of 0.04 is deterministic. It would happen the same way every time. Whether gene flow helps or harms depends on what the new alleles do in the new place.
scenes.visual: A frequency line with a resident marker and an immigrant marker; the resident marker slides toward the immigrants and lands at the weighted mean; the same move repeats identically; two gene-flow outcome chips appear.

scenes.tts: Now sample. The next generation is made by drawing two hundred gene copies at random. The expected frequency stays at zero point five six. Drift adds no push in either direction. But single outcomes scatter around it, by about three and a half points. With only twenty copies, the scatter is about eleven points. Ten times fewer copies gives about three times the scatter.
scenes.caption: Now sample. The next generation is made by drawing 200 gene copies at random. The expected frequency stays at 0.56. Drift adds no push in either direction. But single outcomes scatter around it, by about 3.5 points. With only 20 copies, the scatter is about 11 points. Ten times fewer copies gives about three times the scatter.
scenes.visual: A frequency axis with a fixed expected line at 0.56; outcome dots from 200 copies cluster tightly, then outcome dots from 20 copies spread widely; scatter brackets are drawn.
scenes.narration: Now sample. The next generation is made by drawing 200 gene copies at random. The expected frequency stays at 0.56. Drift adds no push in either direction. scenes.tts: Back to Buri's lines. Any one line wanders. Across one hundred and seven lines, the frequencies spread toward zero and one, while the pooled frequency showed no systematic change. Spread without a shift in the mean is the drift prediction. That fits drift, though it is not proof of it. Buri also asked how large an ideal population would have to be to spread that fast. His mean answer was nine point zero, not sixteen. Buri said the cause was not known. He judged that variation in how many offspring each fly left, down to complete sterility, was certainly part of it, and thought crowding for egg laying space probably played a role. Either way, chance acted on fewer effective parents.

scenes.tts: Suppose an allele is common on an island and rare on the mainland. Three explanations make three predictions. Drift predicts that replicates scatter in both directions, with a mean that stays at the start. Selection predicts that replicates tend to shift the same way on average, and carriers do better in a fitness test. Gene flow predicts frequencies that track the amount and source of immigration. A neutral null is a model of what chance alone would produce. So keep this rule. Use replicates, a neutral null, and an independent fitness assay.
